limitations.no_genre_field: MAME's -listxml output has NO genre, category or 'is this gambling' field of any kind. The only signal the XML carries about what a machine IS is the driver source file it is implemented in, so the gambling/fruit-machine exclusion below is a hand-curated list of driver paths and nothing more. It is therefore incomplete by construction: a gambling title implemented in a shared or misc driver is not detectable here and will pass the filter. Category data lives in catver.ini, which is a separate community-maintained file with its own licence and cadence; ingesting it is a roadmap item, not part of this stage. Do not add a heuristic over machine descriptions to paper over this — 'Poker' appears in the description of plenty of non-gambling arcade titles, and a false positive silently deletes a board from the dataset.
limitations.ismechanical_is_mame_s_word: MAME sets ismechanical on machines whose primary output is a physical mechanism (pinball, redemption, slot cabinets). It overlaps the gambling exclusion but does not contain it: a video slot machine with no moving parts is not mechanical.

known_schema_violations_note: Every entry above is one defect, stated ten times because the mechanism is per row. schemas/schema.sql's `sourcefile` grammar (docs/data-model.md §3.2) is `^[a-z0-9_]+(?:/[a-z0-9_]+)*\.cpp$`, which does not admit a hyphen. MAME 0.288 ships 29 distinct driver paths that contain one — konami/nwk-tr.cpp, sega/315-6154.cpp, devices/machine/pci-ide.cpp and so on — and ten of them belong to machines that survive this filter. The data is correct and the grammar is wrong; the fix is to admit '-' in the sourcefile grammar (and in schemas/common.schema.json's matching pattern), after which these ten entries become unused and the run says so. Until then they are acknowledged here so that a NEW disagreement between MAME and the DDL still fails the build. This list is not a mute button: anything not named here fails.
